summary: Parks Canada heritage statement dates the two-storey Summit Fire Lookout on Mount Revelstoke to 1927; a 1930 report shows a fire ranger in charge and a motor road to the summit.

facts.design: Two-storey wood frame cupola-style lookout cabin with shingle and clapboard cladding, a square cupola with windows on all sides, and a design based on a United States Forest Service model

access.note: The heritage register calls the lookout a prominent attraction that yearly visitors know. No source I could open says whether the cabin's interior is open to the public.

events.note: Constructed at the summit of Mount Revelstoke by the Dominion Forestry Branch, per the Parks Canada heritage statement.
The lookout station, in charge of Fire Ranger Chas. Kolofsky, began registering visitors on June 19, 1930. By July 18, 126 people had come up the 20-mile motor highway to the summit.

corrections.why: The register and the heritage statement both describe a two-storey wood-frame cabin with a cupola, not a tower.

notes_for_editor: The 1927 build date and Dominion Forestry Branch builder come from the Parks Canada heritage statement, read over plain http because the https host failed certificate checks in the fetch tool; the source URL is the http one, so the editor may want to swap it for an https copy. The HistoricPlaces.ca text I could read is a fragment with no date, so the story says the description is undated. The current status is unconfirmed: the standing status rests on the register and heritage text, and no page dated after them was opened. The Parks Canada summit pages (Meadows in the Sky Parkway, summit short hikes) appeared only as search snippets and are not quoted, so current public access to the lookout is unverified. The heritage statement says a federal designation exists, but the year is not in the text I read, so no designation event is recorded. The brief's Parks Canada agency matches the heritage statement. Read budget: 6 page reads and 2 searches.
